name: Neovim
summary: Neovim accepts AI-assisted contributions, but the human must review, understand and steer the AI's output rather than sending one-shot AI pull requests. AI-written text such as PR descriptions, commit messages and documentation must be concise and free of AI padding; ignoring the AI guidance gets the PR closed and can get the author blocked from the organization.

evidence.quote: You are expected to review the generated code yourself, understand it, ask your AI questions and guide it through improvements and refinements that consider the "whole picture".
Review the output yourself before sending a non-Draft PR. Do NOT request review until YOU have checked the AI generated code.
AI work is only valuable if you, the human, review it and ask questions to drive further improvements. Do not send AI "one-shot" PRs.
AI is more valuable when it's guided by you, the human, with the goal of producing elegant code that fits the project vision, conventions, and architecture.
REMOVE verbosity and blathering from documentation, comments, PR description, commit message, etc. All resources, including names, should be CONCISE and CLEAR.
REMOVE and DEDUPLICATE redundant code, tests, explanations, etc. Explicitness and clarity are GOOD but verbosity, over-explanation, and redundancy is BAD.
REMOVE verbosity and blathering from documentation, comments, PR description, commit message, etc. All resources, including names, should be CONCISE and CLEAR.

If your PR description includes noise such as a "Testing" section with excruciating detail about how the AI tested the code (completely useless for reviewers: we have CI), that indicates you didn't understand the above guidance; your PR will be closed and you will be blocked from the org.
Before sending a PR, read [AI-assisted work](#ai-assisted-work), otherwise your PR will be closed and you may be blocked from the org.
